intent: One top-level entry of a NavigationMenu, holding either a trigger with its content or a single direct link.
typical_uses: An entry that expands, holding a NavigationMenuTrigger and its NavigationMenuContent
An entry that navigates directly, holding one NavigationMenuLink

dont_use_when.situation: A link inside an open panel

instead.note: Links inside a NavigationMenuContent need no item of their own; the item is only for the list's top-level entries.

invariants.text: The item's `value` is what the root's value is compared against to decide which item is open; without one, the item generates a unique value of its own, so `value` is needed only when the caller sets the root's `value` or `defaultValue`.
The trigger, the content, the NavigationMenuIcon and the NavigationMenuIndicator read which item they belong to from the nearest NavigationMenuItem, and all four throw when rendered outside one.

anti_patterns.dont: Put two NavigationMenuTrigger parts in one item
anti_patterns.do_instead: Give every trigger its own item; an item carries one value, so both triggers would open the same content

value.states: value is an opaque identifier, typed any by Base UI, compared by identity against the root's value
value.because: Base UI's NavigationMenu.Item declares `value?: any` - not interpreted, only compared by identity, so no JSON Schema type can state what it holds.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the item's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property; the primitive passes an empty state object.

style.states: style accepts a function as well as a plain style object; the primitive passes that function an empty state object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)`, and the item's state carries no fields. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through navigation-menu.module.css, not through this.

good.title: An expanding entry with a controlled value
An expanding entry with its tracking arrow

bad.title: Two triggers sharing one item
bad.why: Both triggers read the same item value, so either one opens the same content and the second entry has no panel of its own.
